summary.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16% and EBITDA 26% YoY; management targets new products (poles, towers, guardrails) at 25-30% of revenue this year.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue up 16% YoY and EBITDA up 26%, with H2 revenue up 18% and EBITDA up 21%. The call centred on diversification: the Jharsuguda (Odisha) unit now produces highway guardrails, octagon and high-mast poles, and transmission line towers, with about 2,300-2,400 tons of tower orders on the books. Management said new products carry higher margins than pipe, but EBITDA margin remains around 4% today. Capex is limited to about Rs 10 crore in FY27, with no new debt planned, and CRISIL upgraded the rating from BBB to BBB+.

segments.name: Pipe (black and galvanized, water line)
segments.commentary: About 85% of revenue and the largest volume product; management ranks it lowest on margin per ton. Pipe installed capacity exceeds utilisation, with a 10-15% per year utilisation increase targeted; Jharsuguda pipe expected to reach about 60% in 1.5-2 years.

segments.name: Highway guardrail / crash barrier
segments.commentary: About 12% of revenue; Hyderabad order book about twice production capacity, and a second galvanizing line is being added there. Current crash barrier orders about 2,000 tons (about 1,000 each in Hyderabad and Jharsuguda).

segments.name: Transmission line towers
segments.commentary: Early-stage; about 2,300-2,400 tons of orders mainly from Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh, with a target of 1,000 tons per month. Management says capacity and orders are roughly equal today; the orders are expected to clear in about two months.

segments.name: Octagon and high-mast poles / monopole
segments.commentary: Pole capacity about 150 tons, with machines arriving in about 10 days to lift it to 300 tons and a target of 500 tons per month this year. Order book about 300 tons, with orders being held for about 45 days; monopole certification expected by Q2 FY27.

guidance_outlook: New products (poles, towers, guardrails) targeted at 25-30% of revenue this year, versus 15% today.
Management said EBITDA margin should rise by at least 1% above the current 4%, and called its figures conservative; steel price swings and new-product pricing are the key variables.
Revenue target of around Rs 1,300-1,400 crore, with management calling this subjective; an analyst's FY28 Rs 1,700 crore reference was not confirmed.
Pole target of 500 tons per month; tower target of 1,000 tons per month; EBITDA margin on new products estimated at about 7-8%, not yet verified.
No new debt planned for FY27-28; capex about Rs 10 crore in FY27, to be spent only when demand is confirmed.
Jharsuguda galvanizing tank to be added in about 1-1.5 months; Hyderabad galvanizing expansion also underway.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity about 3,77,000 MT per annum: Maharashtra (Bombay) about 1,25,000 tons at 74% utilisation; Hyderabad about 96,000 tons at 67%; Jharsuguda is the growth site.
Galvanizing lines in Maharashtra and Hyderabad are described as running at about 100% of installed galvanizing capacity.
Jharsuguda: second galvanizing tank being installed in about 1-1.5 months (machines arrived, civil work ongoing); Hyderabad adding another galvanizing line for crash barriers.
Pole capacity to go from 150 to 300 tons with machines arriving in about 10 days, targeting 500 tons per month this year; monopole certification pending with CPRI.
FY27 capex about Rs 10 crore, to be spent only once demand is confirmed (for example, poles going from 500 to 800-1,000 tons).
demand_pricing: Pipe price: about Rs 52,000 per ton last year (black), now about Rs 65,000 per ton; management said steel prices could rise further if geopolitical tensions persist.
Order book: about 5,000 tons of pipe across all three units (about 2,000 Maharashtra, 1,800 Hyderabad), expected to be delivered within about 4 days.
Jindal Steel offtake agreement runs April 2023 to March 2029 with a minimum offtake of 1 lakh metric tons; the company produces ERW pipe for Jindal.

Middle East conflict raised transportation and furnace oil costs (galvanizing uses furnace oil); exports to Europe disrupted, with a shift to Australia shipped from Bombay. Management says costs are being passed through to customers so far.
Management says India demand is growing about 9% a year in utilisation, and the company has PWD registrations in Chhattisgarh and UP for poles and towers.
Management said that the new products are order-based, so they are less exposed to steel-price inventory swings than pipe.

qa_highlights.question: What EBITDA margin is expected at the Rs 1,700 crore revenue level by FY28, given 4% today?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said new products (monopole, octagon/high-mast poles, towers, guardrails) carry higher margins than pipe, so margin should exceed 4% by at least 1%; tower orders are at about Rs 10,000 per ton margin versus Rs 3,000-4,000 per ton on galvanized pipe.

qa_highlights.question: Why is EBITDA per ton on galvanized pipe (about Rs 3,000) well below some peers (Rs 6,000-7,000)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said its figures are conservative and that the company makes water-line pipe, while peers make higher-margin API pipe and export, which Vibhor is not targeting.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue and EBITDA contribution from new products in FY26, and what margin can they reach?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined an exact FY26 figure, saying the products are new; it targets 25-30% of revenue from new products and estimates new-product EBITDA margin at about 7-8%, not yet verified.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any impact from the Middle East war?
qa_highlights.answer: Transport costs and furnace oil prices have risen and are being passed on to customers; export to Europe is disrupted and redirected to Australia, but domestic demand is said to be healthy.

qa_highlights.question: What are the current order book and delivery timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: Pipe about 5,000 tons (delivered within about 4 days); crash barriers about 2,000 tons (about one month); towers about 2,400 tons (about two months, given audit and inspection); poles about 300 tons (about 45 days).

qa_highlights.question: Was there any one-off or inventory gain in FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO said inventory gains are a regular process since finished product prices are reset monthly, so there is no major exceptional item; management said steel price spikes around the US-Iran conflict may reflect in Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What capex is planned for FY27, and what is the debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: About Rs 10 crore of capex in FY27, to be deployed only when demand is confirmed, and no new debt, as existing financing is already in place.

risks_watch: Margin uplift from new products depends on pricing for a new entrant; management said current prices are not a premium, and the 7-8% margin estimate is unverified.
Steel price volatility; inventory gains on pipe could reverse, and management flagged the Middle East conflict as a driver.
Pipe utilisation is well below installed capacity (Jharsuguda target 60% in 1.5-2 years), and pipe remains about 85% of revenue.
Monopole certification from CPRI is pending, with expected clearance by Q2 FY27; several department permissions are still pending.
Export disruption to Europe, plus higher freight and furnace oil costs from the Middle East conflict.
Concentration: Jindal offtake agreement (minimum 1 lakh MT per year) and tower orders tied to a few state electricity customers.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on diversification and order flow, with repeated emphasis on conservative guidance. Management was vague or deferred on hard numbers (FY26 new-product revenue, peak revenue at current capacity, product-wise margins), and attributed margin and revenue uncertainty to steel price volatility.
